items.informal_name: Vandermonde Determinant Non-Zero If and Only If Vector is Injective
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {n : ℕ} [IsDomain R] {v : Fin n → R},
  (Matrix.vandermonde v).det ≠ 0 ↔ Function.Injective v
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be a commutative ring with no zero divisors (a domain), and let $ v : \mathrm{Fin}(n) \to R $ be a vector of length $ n $. The determinant of the $ n \times n $ Vandermonde matrix constructed from $ v $, whose $(i,j)$-entry is $ v_i^j $, is non-zero if and only if the function $ v $ is injective (i.e., all elements $ v_0, v_1, \ldots, v_{n-1} $ are distinct in $ R $).

items.informal_name: Determinant of Vandermonde Matrix is Zero iff Two Entries are Equal
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {n : ℕ} [IsDomain R] {v : Fin n → R},
  (Matrix.vandermonde v).det = 0 ↔ ∃ i j, v i = v j ∧ i ≠ j
items.informal_description: For a domain $ R $ and a vector $ v $ of length $ n $ with entries in $ R $, the determinant of the Vandermonde matrix $ V $ formed by $ v $ is zero if and only if there exist distinct indices $ i, j $ such that $ v_i = v_j $.

items.informal_name: Non-vanishing Determinant of Square Matrix of Variables in Multivariate Polynomial Ring
items.type:
∀ (m : Type u_1) (R : Type u_3) [inst : DecidableEq m] [inst_1 : Fintype m] [inst_2 : CommRing R] [Nontrivial R],
  (Matrix.mvPolynomialX m m R).det ≠ 0
items.informal_description: Given a finite type $ m $ with decidable equality and a non-trivial commutative ring $ R $, the determinant of the $ m \times m $ matrix whose $(i,j)$-entries are distinct indeterminates $ X_{(i,j)} $ in the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[X_{(i,j)}] $ is non-zero. This holds because the determinant evaluates to a monomial that cannot be zero in the polynomial ring over a non-trivial ring.

items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n → R),
  (Matrix.vandermonde v).det = ∏ i, ∏ j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, (v j - v i)
items.informal_description: The determinant of the Vandermonde matrix constructed from a vector $ v $ of length $ n $ with entries in a commutative ring $ R $ is equal to the product of $ (v_j - v_i) $ for all $ 0 \leq i < j < n $. Formally, $ \det(\text{vandermonde}(v)) = \prod_{0 \leq i < j < n} (v_j - v_i) $.

items.informal_name: Vandermonde Determinant Equals Monic Polynomial Evaluation Determinant
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n → R) (p : Fin n → Polynomial R),
  (∀ (i : Fin n), (p i).natDegree = ↑i) →
    (∀ (i : Fin n), (p i).Monic) → (Matrix.vandermonde v).det = (Matrix.of fun i j => Polynomial.eval (v i) (p j)).det
items.informal_description: For a commutative ring $ R $, a vector $ v $ of length $ n $ with entries in $ R $, and a sequence of monic polynomials $ p_0, p_1, \ldots, p_{n-1} $ over $ R $ where each $ p_i $ has degree $ i $, the determinant of the $ n \times n $ Vandermonde matrix formed by $ v $ is equal to the determinant of the matrix whose $ (i,j) $-entry is $ p_j(v_i) $, the evaluation of polynomial $ p_j $ at $ v_i $. This equality holds under the conditions that each polynomial is monic and has natural degree equal to its index.

items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] {n : ℕ} (v w : Fin n → R),
  (Matrix.projVandermonde v w).det = ∏ i, ∏ j ∈ Finset.Ioi i, (v j * w i - v i * w j)
items.informal_description: The determinant of the $n \times n$ generalized Vandermonde matrix with entries $(v_i^j w_i^{n-1-j})$ is equal to the product over all $0 \le i < j < n$ of $(v_j w_i - v_i w_j)$, i.e., $\det(\text{Vandermonde}(v,w)) = \prod_{0 \le i < j < n} (v_j w_i - v_i w_j)$.
